requirement: POST, PUT, and DELETE operations on a dish are restricted to the dish's owner; other authenticated users are denied (any user may GET).
label: GAP
evidence: Authentication is enforced globally in require_authentication()/validate_token(), but POST /dishes in dishes_collection() creates dishes without storing any owner field, and PUT/DELETE in dish_resource() perform update/delete after only checking existence. There is no code comparing request.auth_data to a dish owner, and GET is not exempted from authentication.
reasoning: The requirement is specifically that POST, PUT, and DELETE on a dish are restricted to the dish's owner, while any user may GET. The code has no ownership model at all: dishes do not store an owner and modifying routes do not authorize against one, so there is no behavior addressing owner-only access control. Per the decision guide, because the required behavior is absent entirely rather than merely incorrect in detail, the label is GAP.
